Today, the agency approved a first-of-its-kind treatment for adults with chronic hepatitis B, a viral infection of the liver that can lead to cirrhosis and liver cancer. The drug is given as a monthly injection and works by silencing viral genes within infected cells. In two clinical trials involving 1,150 participants, a significantly higher proportion of those who received the drug achieved sustained suppression of the virus compared with those who received standard therapy. The most common side effects were injection site reactions, headache, and fatigue. “This approval offers a new option for patients who have long needed one,” said the director of the relevant office. The agency granted the application priority review. The sponsor must complete a post-marketing study to assess long-term liver outcomes.
